sections.title: Writing Books
sections.text: Each folder directly under docs/ becomes a book. Its Markdown files become chapters. Loose Markdown files directly in docs/ share a separate book. Nested folders stay in the same book by default, with their index.md introducing each chapter group. docs/ ├── index.md # Book of loose Markdown files ├── notes.md └── handbook/ # Another book ├── index.md # Book introduction ├── setup.md └── examples/ # Chapter group within handbook ├── index.md # Group introduction └── cli.md Title search appears with seven or more books. It also appears in smaller libraries if any book has a category or publication date.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Chapters and sections
sections.text: Each folder starts with its index.md. Set the order of what follows in that file's YAML front matter. chapters: - setup.md - examples/ - reference.md Listed chapters and folders come first. Unlisted items follow in natural filename order (2 before 10), which is also the default without chapters. A nested folder uses its own index.md to order its contents. Entries must name direct Markdown files or folders in the same book. Missing entries, duplicates, and deeper paths stop the build with the affected index.md in the error. Chapter filenames and URLs stay unchanged. Use H1 for the chapter title. An H2 opens a new page. When the first H2 immediately follows the chapter title, they share the first page. Use H3 for subheadings within a page. The table of contents groups H2 sections and their page numbers under each chapter.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Titles, links, and covers
sections.text: The H1 in the book's index.md names the book. Keep your paths in English and write titles in your readers' language. Set locale: ja in grimoire.yml to display the reader controls in Japanese. Link to other chapters with relative Markdown paths and an optional heading anchor. For example, [Drawings](./media.md#mermaid-diagrams) opens the Mermaid section. You can also copy a chapter or section URL directly from the reader. Set the cover in the book's index.md front matter. Available covers are red, green, blue, plum, amber, teal, black, ivory, walnut, and slate. Books without a cover setting use a color based on their folder path. --- cover: teal --- # Release Notes

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Categories and publication dates
sections.text: Use category in a book's index.md to place it with related books under a labeled shelf plate. The library also lets readers filter by category. To give a nested folder its own book, set book: true in that folder's index.md. For example, put the following in docs/system/data/index.md to move its chapters into Data Models. Give docs/system/index.md the same category to place both books on the System shelf. --- book: true title: Data Models category: System --- # Data Models --- category: Experiments date: "2026-11-19" --- # Field Notes Both fields are optional. Use any category name and a date in YYYY-MM-DD format. The category selector appears if at least one book has a category. The sort selector appears if at least one book has a publication date. The selectors work with title search and carry across Shelves and Index. Newest first lists dated books first, with same-day books in title order and undated books at the end. Default order restores folder order on the shelves and title order in the index. Chapter order comes from the files in each book.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Custom cover artwork
sections.text: Set coverImage in the book's index.md to show your own artwork on the front of its book on the shelves. --- cover: green coverImage: ./assets/field-notes.webp --- # Field Notes Use an AVIF, GIF, JPEG, PNG, or WebP file anywhere under docs/. Paths are relative to the book's index.md. The image fits below the title without cropping. Long titles use up to three lines on the cover, and the book link keeps its full title. Use a small, compressed image for a fast bookshelf.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.text: Each syntax example is followed by its rendered result. Use H1 for a chapter title, H2 for a new page, and H3 for a heading within a page.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Paper marks
sections.text: **Bold**, *italics*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code` :underline[Underline], :highlight[highlight], :red[red ink] Bold, italics, strikethrough, inline code Underline, highlight, red ink Marks keep the paper's serif type. Highlights use pale gold; red ink uses a muted burgundy.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Block quotes and attribution
sections.text: > What does not kill me makes me stronger. > > *— Friedrich Nietzsche* What does not kill me makes me stronger. — Friedrich Nietzsche A thin gold rule and inset mark the quoted passage without adding a background. Write the attribution as ordinary italics. Quotes can contain multiple paragraphs, nested quotes, links, and lists.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Callouts
sections.text: > [!NOTE] > Keep a copy of the original Markdown and images. [!NOTE] Keep a copy of the original Markdown and images. Unlike ordinary quotes, callouts have a label and a shaded background. [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], and [!CAUTION] also work. Labels follow the site's locale setting.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Lists
sections.text: - First item - A nested note - Next item 9. Review the manuscript 10. Publish the site First item A nested note Next item Review the manuscript Publish the site Bullets and numbers use muted gold. Nested bullets become hollow circles, and wrapped lines align with the item text. Ordered lists keep the starting number written in Markdown, including two-digit numbers.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Task lists
sections.text: - [x] Write the manuscript - [ ] Publish the site Write the manuscript Publish the site Small gold boxes show the progress recorded in the source. Readers cannot edit them on the page; the author updates [x] in Markdown.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Horizontal rules
sections.text: The previous topic. --- The next topic. The previous topic. The next topic. A fine gold line with a small central diamond separates topics within the same page.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Collapsible notes
sections.text: <details><summary>Read the extra notes</summary> **Additional explanation** goes here. </details> Read the extra notes Additional explanation goes here. Select the triangle and heading to reveal an indented note. Use Tab to focus it, then Enter or Space to toggle it. Blank lines around the contents allow Markdown inside. Use <details open> to start expanded. Scripts and event attributes are removed.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Math
sections.text: An inline equation: $E = mc^2$. $$ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$ An inline equation: E = mc^2. x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $...$ stays in the text line. A separate $$ block is centered. Long display equations scroll horizontally within the paper. Equations are included in the published HTML and remain readable without JavaScript.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Definition lists
sections.text: Chapter : A group of content from one Markdown file. Page : A sheet separated by an H2 heading. Chapter A group of content from one Markdown file. Page A sheet separated by an H2 heading. Terms appear in bold, with their definitions indented beneath them. Use this format for a glossary or API terminology.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Syntax highlighting
sections.text: ```typescript const title: string = "Grimoire"; console.log(title); ``` const title: string = "Grimoire"; console.log(title); Add a language name to a code fence for muted colors that suit the paper: burgundy keywords, olive strings, and darker ink for the rest. Unknown languages remain plain text. A mermaid fence still produces a diagram.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Footnotes
sections.text: Check the original source[^source]. [^source]: Research notes saved with the manuscript. Check the original source. Research notes saved with the manuscript. Select the small reference number to reach the note at the end of the page. Select its return arrow to go back to the reference. Footnotes remain available on the page that uses them when H2 headings split a chapter into sheets.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Tables and matrices
sections.text: | Format | Result | | --- | --- | | Markdown | Text | | Mermaid | Diagram | [Media examples](./media.md) Format Result Markdown Text Mermaid Diagram Media examples On a narrow page, the table scrolls horizontally while its first column stays visible. Relative chapter links and heading anchors also work.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Spell Mode
sections.text: Set magicMode: true in grimoire.yml to show the toggle. Highlights draw across the words, bold text lifts, and strikethrough strokes appear. Effects play once when a page comes into view and respect the device's reduced-motion setting.

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.text: Use Markdown image syntax for still images, animated GIFs, and MP4 files. Resolve local paths from the chapter that uses them. The static build bundles referenced local media.

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: Images and GIFs
sections.text: Use AVIF, WebP, PNG, JPEG, or GIF. Write an alt description inside the brackets. Click or tap an image in the reader to enlarge it. Zoom in to inspect details, choose Fit to see the whole image, or close the viewer to resume reading. ![From Markdown to a static site](../assets/diagram.avif) ![The publishing flow in motion](../assets/publishing-flow.gif) From Markdown to a static site The publishing flow in motion

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: MP4
sections.text: An MP4 renders as a video player inside the page. Playback pauses when you turn away from it. ![Publishing flow video](../assets/publishing-flow.mp4) Publishing flow video

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: YouTube and Vimeo
sections.text: Use the video URL in the same syntax. The embedded player loads when the reader selects it. The source link still works when the video owner restricts embedding. ![YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M7lc1UVf-VE) ![Vimeo demo](https://vimeo.com/76979871) YouTube demo Vimeo demo

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: Mermaid diagrams
sections.text: Set the language of a fenced code block to mermaid. Select the diagram to open the viewer, then zoom and drag to explore. You can also pan with the arrow keys and press Escape to return to the page. flowchart LR subgraph Source Markdown[Markdown chapters] Settings[Project settings] Art[Images and video] end subgraph Build Books[Sort books and chapters] Paper[Split pages at H2] Links[Resolve links and media] end subgraph Output Library[Library] Chapters[Chapter HTML] Sitemap[Sitemap] end Markdown --> Books --> Paper --> Chapters Art --> Links --> Chapters Settings --> Library Settings --> Sitemap Books --> Library
